summary: On the main deck a SYSTEM ALARM SOUNDS again. Tank reports that the attackers have breached the outer hull ("They've burned through the outer hull."), and Trinity urges Neo to hurry ("Hurry, Neo."), indicating the hull breach has tightened the time pressure on Neo's simultaneous effort elsewhere.

what_changes.before: The hovercraft's outer hull is intact and holding.
what_changes.after: The attackers have burned through the outer hull, so the ship is now compromised.
what_changes.evidence: Another SYSTEM ALARM SOUNDS. TANK They've burned through the outer hull.

event_hint.one_line: During the Sentinels' assault on the hovercraft, the outer hull is breached while Neo races to finish his task.

minds.wants: To deliver the one piece of operational information that changes what everyone else must do — that the last barrier is gone.
minds.feels: A cold, disciplined alarm: the breach he's been tracking and dreading has become a fact, and with it the knowledge that their margin has collapsed. He is frightened but has converted the fear entirely into a status report rather than a reaction.
minds.shows: A flat, technical sentence — "They've burned through the outer hull" — no panic, no plea, just the data. He lets the fact speak for itself.
minds.basis: The scene opens on "Another SYSTEM ALARM SOUNDS," which the facts mark as recurring ("again"), and Tank responds with a declarative observation of hull compromise rather than any emotional outburst. His role throughout the hovercraft scenes has been monitoring/operating the ship's systems, so reporting a breach is exactly his function.

believes_about.belief: That stating the breach plainly is enough — that they will instantly understand the implication (there is almost no time left) without him having to spell out urgency or fear.
believes_about.wrong_because: He cannot know whether Trinity registers the full stakes or whether Neo, absorbed in his simultaneous task, even hears him; the bare report may land as more or less catastrophic than he intends.

minds.wants: To compress whatever time is left into Neo finishing his task — to turn the bad news into acceleration rather than panic.
minds.feels: Terror that the ship is now exposed and that Neo is still vulnerable/occupied, but she refuses to spend a single instant on the fear itself; every ounce of it is redirected into a command.
minds.shows: Two words, an imperative — "Hurry, Neo" — addressed past Tank to Neo. She does not react to Tank's report, does not look at the danger; she answers it with motion.
minds.basis: Against Tank's report of the hull breach, her only line is an urge to Neo to speed up rather than any acknowledgment of the breach — the facts explicitly read this as the breach tightening time pressure on Neo. Her established pattern (watching Morpheus in sc-204, later holding and reviving Neo per the event shape) is to meet catastrophe with focused action, not with visible distress.

believes_about.belief: That he can still be hurried — that more speed is within his control and will be enough to get him out before the Sentinels reach them.
believes_about.wrong_because: She cannot see Neo's actual state or how close the Sentinels truly are; the breach may have already closed the gap beyond what any hurry can fix. Her belief that urgency is still useful is a wager, not a known fact.

believes_about.belief: That Tank's report is simply the trigger she needed and that no further exchange is required between them right now.
believes_about.wrong_because: Tank may be looking to her for a decision or a shared acknowledgment of how bad this is; by answering only Neo, she leaves his need for a response unmet.

connects_back: The recurring SYSTEM ALARM ('again') continues the Sentinel assault already underway across the preceding hovercraft scenes.
Tank's role as the ship's systems operator, established in earlier hovercraft scenes, grounds why he names the breach.
Trinity's action-first response to crisis echoes her watchful, steady presence in sc-204 and her role in the event shape (holding/reviving Neo).
The time pressure on Neo connects to his race up the fire escape and through the hall in sc-205–sc-206.
sets_up: The breached hull makes the imminent Sentinel boarding real, forcing the crew toward the EMP as the only remaining counter (ev-035).
The collapsed margin is what makes Neo's rush to the exit phone and his unplugging urgent and barely-in-time (ev-035).
Trinity's fixation on getting Neo to finish/hurry prefigures her presence at his side when he wakes back on the ship (ev-035).
dramatic_function: To convert the abstract threat of the assault into an irreversible, concrete fact — the hull is gone — so that the scene's tension shifts from 'can Neo make it in time' to 'there is almost no time left,' tightening the screw on Neo's parallel effort without spending a word on fear.
